## Purpose

Explicitly answer an accepted input with `aq supervisor-inbox reply
--conversation-id <id> --input-id <id> --idempotency-key <key>` and exactly one of
`--text <answer>` or `--file <UTF-8-path>`.

## When a playbook uses it

Only the local operator or the authenticated live global supervisor launch may
reply. A project-scoped supervisor, stale launch, worker, service or playbook
principal is refused. Generic message sends and transcript tails do not relay replies.

## How it works internally

[`conversation_commands.py`](../../../src/commands/conversation_commands.py)
checks the live session instance, input binding and destination. It persists an
answer and input reply pointer before queuing the bounded, mention-free Discord
render. The contract redacts reply text. Reusing the same conversation and
idempotency key returns the first durable answer with `created: false`.

## Side effects and persistence

Writes a conversation reply message, marks the input answered and queues a
`conv-reply:` outbox delivery. The full answer is durable; the Discord render is
bounded to 1,900 characters including its marker and dashboard pointer.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

Refusals include `out_of_scope`, `spoofed_identity`, `invalid_request`,
`conversation_not_found`, `input_not_in_conversation`, `conversation_closed`,
`input_revoked` and `preconditions_unmet`. Use status for readiness and history for
verified input and reply pointers. Retry with the same idempotency key after a
transient enqueue failure.

## Example step

The operator supplies `--file answer.md` and a stable key for one answer. A retry
uses that same key; a different answer uses a new key after inspecting history.
